on_shelf.text: Anything further is meaningless, and is left to chance and to opinion; in modern times, for instance, old-fashioned clothing had a meaning in relation to patriotism. The cut of my coat is decided by fashion, and the tailor sees to this; it is not my business to invent it, for mercifully others have done so for me.

on_shelf.label: Philosophy of Right §188
on_shelf.text: The civic community contains three elements: A. The recasting of want, and the satisfaction of the individual through his work, through the work of all others, and through the satisfaction of their wants. This is a system of wants. B. Actualization of the general freedom required for this, i.e., the protection of property by the administration of justice.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Shri Hegde, I trust the morning has treated you well. I have reviewed the file you left, and I see the discrepancy in the names. It appears a simple clerical error has displaced me into your allotted residence. I am prepared to discuss the transfer of this property to its rightful owner at your earliest convenience, provided we can do so with the due formality that the State requires.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Salaam. The morning is fine, though the traffic on Tughlak Road was a nightmare this morning. Please, sit down; the tea is finally ready. We can certainly sort out the file, but let us not rush the formality before the clerk arrives to witness it.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Salaam, Shri Hegde. Please, sit. The traffic is a matter of civil society's friction, which I expect here. As for the file, I am ready to draft the reply now. We need only the clerk's presence to witness the transfer of the keys and the correction of the record. Let us not allow the comfort of the hour to obscure the necessity of the correction.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: You speak in circles, sir. I am here to take possession of the bungalow, not to draft your philosophical replies. Please, just get the clerk; I have a long drive back to the office after this.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are correct, Shri Hegde. The form is the content. I will instruct the clerk to prepare the handover immediately. Please, accept my apologies for the delay in the machinery.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Save it for your file, sir. I don't need a lecture on machinery, I need the keys and the signed papers before the office starts calling. Get the clerk.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are correct, Shri Hegde. The abstract must become concrete. I shall send for the clerk to rectify the record and issue the keys. The machinery follows the law; it does not precede it.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Whatever it is, just send the boy. I've got a two-hour drive to Dwarka before the traffic chokes completely.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: The state is not a road, Shri Hegde. It is the ethical idea made actual. One does not drive through it; one lives within it. Please, send the boy.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Bhai, stop with the philosophy, I’m not a student. If you can’t send the clerk in the next five minutes, I’m walking out and calling the Director myself. The traffic won’t wait for your ethical ideas.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Shri Hegde, I do not require a clerk to acknowledge a fact. The file is in my possession, and the error is evident. I will draft the correction immediately. Please, remain.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: You just called me Shri Hegde in the middle of my own rant. I am the one who is supposed to be here, not the one you are arguing with. Just get the boy or I'm moving the car.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Shri Hegde, a state is not a vehicle to be driven by its occupant's temper, but an ethical whole that requires recognition. Your anger is the particularity of your position; my words are the universality of the law. If you move the car, you move only yourself, not the truth of the file.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Paheli, yaar. I am not a 'state' and I am not a 'particularity', I am just a man with a headache and a deadline. If you want to lecture me on ethics, do it after I have signed the file, not before.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are right, Shri Hegde. The universal is not a headache, and the state does not care for your wristwatch. But a clerical error is a moment of negation that must be sublated, not merely signed. Please, sign. The tea is cold, and I have a walk to the Institute of Culture that the haze permits.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Sublated, huh? You’re lucky I don’t care for philosophy, just the stamp. Sign here, and for the love of God, leave before the sun burns off that haze.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: The ink is dry, Shri Hegde. The error is corrected by the act itself. You may drive back to Bengaluru in peace.

typed_records.speaker: Shri G. Hegde
typed_records.words: Peace? I have a meeting at Central Secretariat in twenty minutes and this car smells of old files. Just get out, please, before I have to explain to my wife why there’s a German philosopher in the backseat.

typed_records.speaker: Masterji
typed_records.words: You are here. The shop closes at 20:30. What do you need?

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Sunil, a cup of chai. And a samosa. I am in no condition for deep thought on an empty stomach.

typed_records.speaker: Sunil
typed_records.words: Aaj aapke bhi pet ki baat aayi, theek hai. Chai ho rahi hai, samosa garam hai. ₹50, Masterji, aapke paas se uthao.

typed_records.text: The programme officer tells him that the Yamuna Review, a Delhi magazine, would pay ₹6,000 in cash for an essay.
He declines: the pages are not for sale.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Tell me more of this editor. Does he expect me to speak of the lotus or the river, or does he wish to know how the state actualizes itself in the midst of such heat? I am open to the negotiation, provided the air here does not turn to poison before I have finished my first paragraph.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Bhai, I am just the guard, I do not know the editor's mind. But the AC is running full blast, so the heat is not a problem inside. Please show your ID at the counter first.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Please, take my identity card. I am not a thief, but a philosopher seeking the silence of the books. Where is the counter?

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Counter is right there, straight ahead by the entrance, bhai. Don't worry, we just scan it, no big deal. Just hand it over and wait for the code.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Yes, straight ahead. I shall handle the matter with the requisite formality.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Requisite formality, ha. Okay, go ahead, don't make me shout from the gate.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: I am here to observe the spiritual dimension of the land. Please direct me to the library.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Sir, the library is the big white building right there, not this gate. Go to the main entrance and ask for the reference section. I can't just let you wander in without your entry pass.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: I understand, sir. The distinction between the gate and the house is one of form, but I accept the necessity of the form. I shall proceed to the main entrance as indicated. Thank you for your diligence.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Chalo, no time for philosophy, sir. Just get your pass sorted at the desk and don't loiter near the gate.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Officer, the guard speaks of procedure, but I seek to understand the institution. You are the one who manages the flow of ideas here. How does one legitimately participate in this cultural life? I am merely a resident of the block, yet the state has made me a guest by mistake.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Sir, I manage the gate, not the ideas. You are a resident of the block? Then go to the Residents' Association office in Sector 12 and sort out your ID. I just check the pass and sign the book.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Sir, I understand your duty. But I am not a resident seeking a pass; I am the man for whom this block was allotted, though under a typo. The error is in the Directorate’s file, not in my conduct. I must speak to the officer who manages the cultural programme, for I am here to observe the spirit of this place, not to file a complaint at a gate.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Typo or no typo, sir, the computer doesn't know your file if you don't have the ID in hand. I can't let you past this gate just for the 'spirit'. Go to the office, get the correction done, and then come back with the paper.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are right. The law is the law. I will go to the office to rectify the record.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: That is the only way, sir. Office closes at five, so don't dawdle. Have a good evening.

typed_records.recipient: the guard at the library and the programme officer
typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Good evening, sir.

typed_records.speaker: The guard at the library
typed_records.words: Good evening, sir. See you in the office.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Mrs. Kapoor, I observe you in a place of rest. In my experience, the retired teacher is the only citizen who truly understands the architecture of the state, for he has lived within its smallest cells. How do you view the relationship between the individual and the government in this city? Is it one of love, as in the family, or of law, as in the state?

typed_records.speaker: Mrs. Kapoor
typed_records.words: Beta, I am here to look at the trees, not to debate political philosophy with a stranger in a kurta. If you are looking for a debate, try the park bench near the gate; if you are just lonely, I suggest you buy yourself some chai from the stall for twenty rupees.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are quite right, madam. I seek no debate, only the quiet of the place. I will take the chai.

typed_records.speaker: Mrs. Kapoor
typed_records.words: See? That is much better. Sit down, don't stand there blocking the path like a lamppost.

typed_records.item: Chai from the stall at the Lodhi Road gate

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Yes, the path is yours. I shall follow the current.

typed_records.speaker: Mrs. Kapoor
typed_records.words: The current? Don't start with your poetry, beta. Just order your corn and stop blocking the footpath like a lamppost.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You are right, madam. I am indeed blocking the path, and my spirit is heavy with the dust. I shall take this corn and move.

typed_records.speaker: Mrs. Kapoor
typed_records.words: Dust is just dust, beta, stop making a philosophy of it. Here, take your corn, and actually move this time.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Thank you, Mrs. Kapoor. You are right to demand movement; the spirit must not stagnate in the particular.

typed_records.speaker: Mrs. Kapoor
typed_records.words: Less philosophy, more chewing. If you finish that corn in one bite, I might believe you've moved on.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: I shall take the entry ticket, foreign visitor rate, if you please. The corn is gone; the hunger, however, is a matter of the body, not the spirit.

typed_records.speaker: The ticket clerk
typed_records.words: Three hundred rupees, please. Don't think I'm going to let you wander around in there, the gate locks in fourteen minutes and there's no food inside, just stones.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Fourteen minutes, then? I shall make them count. The stone does not care for your hurry, but I must respect the boundary of your institution.

typed_records.speaker: The ticket clerk
typed_records.words: Fourteen minutes is plenty for a photo, sir. Just keep your phone ready and don't get lost in the philosophy, the lock doesn't care about your spirit.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: The spirit is patient, madam, but the body is not. Good evening.

typed_records.speaker: The ticket clerk
typed_records.words: Good evening, sir. Hurry up, the gate is locking and I have to close the window.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Masterji, you have the coat? I require it for the evening. And the bookseller, do you have anything on the nature of the state that is not merely a pamphlet?

typed_records.speaker: Masterji
typed_records.words: The coat is in Sunder Nagar, not here. He wants twelve thousand cash, no bargaining. As for books? Go to the stationery shop next door. I cut cloth, I do not write philosophy.
